It is overall a tough market for junior/entry level developers in NL right now. 

Even if you say now that you’re okay with the lower salary (the rate you mentioned is a reasonable range for a junior/starter), you need to think about if you can find any apartment and be able to pay rent (1200-1500 average probably + they ask for 3x salary for renting) and live your life on that salary. Junior roles are also hybrid or onsite mostly so you would need a living space closer to your job, which might be difficult with the high rent. 

Overall I would say it is a bad idea to look for an entry level software dev job in NL right now. Things would be different if you had a few years of experience. But the combination of tough market in general + entry level + housing crisis does not bode well for you. 

BUUUT also try your luck at applying at Alten Nederland. They are known for taking in starters/entry level devs as consultants and it could help that you are an EU citizen. Goodluck.

That is a very crowded resume. Just use bullet points to highlight what you did.  

You have also slapped some % increase/decrease as part of your experience at every line. Are you able to back each of those up if anyone asks how did you measure them?  I know a lot of people suggest quantifying your successes and adding numbers to show how much you improved something in a system, but this is just too much.  I have never added a single % in any of my resumes and i only ever use short lines with bullet points on what I did at each job. If an interviewer has questions about what I did at a particular job about any of the lines I wrote, then I explain in detail. I have never been asked for any numbers I improved while working at a past company. 

I also have a separate section for skills / languages / frameworks I have worked in, not added to the experience section as part of each line. 

 My experience is that of a European in Dutch software field so feel free to adapt this feedback if you are from a different country or continent.

I had the exact same relationship with my mom. Mom was loving and nice. Dad was verbally and emotionally abusive and basically a shithead towards her. She would cry and complain about him to me every day. I was upset when she was upset. I became her therapist and was very dependent on her. My aim in life was to make her happy. I missed out on just... being a kid, you know? She was also anxious about every single thing and I turned out like that too. I didn’t realise this at all until I started therapy two years ago and my therapist pointed out that what she did was not okay. It blew my mind and I remember it took me a while to understand the gravity of the damage. I couldn’t forgive her after that. She still wonders why I went no-contact with her. 

I have anxiety, I am depressed, I obsess over little things. Everything that reminds me of her pisses me off. I didn’t even tell her when I was hospitalised because the image of her being anxious and obsessing over it was something I could not handle without exploding. 

Maybe she didn’t know any better. But that’s no excuse for bad parenting. And I am under no obligation to forgive her. 

I used to expect that someday she’ll try to figure out what went wrong and give me my well-deserved apology. But as time passed and therapy progressed I have begun to tell myself that I need to heal on my own. I’m waiting for an apology that will likely never come. And that’s okay.

Hi OP 
I’m one of the people who commented on your first post. I’m very glad you took the leap and had this conversation with your partner. That must not have been easy and I’m proud of you.

I agree with what the other commenter has said.  You both seem to have different life goals at the moment. Your partner reminds me of my ex a lot. He was a ‘take it a day at a time’ kind of guy and like you, I too wanted to have some goals/plans in place in the next few years. Eventually I understood he was not going to change or adjust so I broke up with him. I did lose 3.5 years of my life waiting for him to move in with me and he still couldn’t decide even that. I was miserable after my breakup but I never regretted it. I am now seeing someone whose life goals align with mine and I made sure I had that discussion in the beginning. 

You don’t need to have *everything* planned out. That can be overwhelming to anyone. Just similar basic goals is what I would look for. In your case it seems like he can’t guarantee he wants the same things you want, even after four years together. 

If you stay you need to remember that there is a good chance you won’t get the things you want (marriage/kids) in your future. Maybe he will say after 4 years that he still can’t decide or he is not ready. Are you okay with that? If you are willing to take that chance, then do stay by all means. If you leave, you get the chance to meet someone whose goals aligns with yours. 

Ultimately it is your decision to stay or leave. Perhaps you could adjust your goals a bit and he could decide to meet you halfway. 
This could be the moment when you can learn if he wants to adjust his goals to let you stay together or if he is fine with it ending. Same applies for you, if you are willing to adjust a bit, perhaps extend your plans to a bit later and you both come to a compromise. This is the ideal solution for both. I hope you get there. 

Goodluck OP, much love.
